articles.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Highly Migratory Species Southeast Data, Assessment, and Review Workshops Advisory Panel
articles.summary: NMFS solicits nominations for the Atlantic Highly Migratory Species (HMS) SouthEast Data, Assessment, and Review (SEDAR) Workshops Advisory Panel, also known as the "SEDAR Pool." The SEDAR Pool is comprised of a group of individuals who, if selected, review data and advise NMFS on the scientific information, data, and models used in stock assessments for oceanic sharks in the Atlantic Ocean, including the Gulf of America and Caribbean Sea. NMFS is seeking nominations for a 5-year term beginning in 2027. NMFS will consider individuals with definable interests in recreational and commercial fishing and related industries, including those from the environmental community, academia, and non-governmental organizations, for membership on the SEDAR Pool.

articles.title: Compliance Procedure (52 U.S.C. 30109, 30107(a))
Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Organ Procurement Organizations Conditions for Coverage: Revisions to the Conditions for Coverage
articles.summary: This final rule revises the Conditions for Coverage for Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs) to clarify outstanding procedural questions and provide additional operational flexibility for OPOs to achieve high performance resulting in the successful procurement, distribution, and transplantation of more life-saving organs. This rule revises definitions, revises the designation requirements for OPOs, clarifies when an OPO's service area is open for competition, and updates the process for appeals. We are committed to holding all OPOs accountable for their performance and this final rule does not revise the focus on improving the volume of donors and transplants assessed in the outcome measures or the tier structure used for re-certification and de-certification of OPOs.

articles.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to approve a revision to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD or "Department") portion of the Arizona State Implementation Plan (SIP). This revision establishes a federally enforceable program allowing for the generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing on-road vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting other Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements. These ERCs are intended to be used as offsets for major stationary sources under the Department's Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) program. The EPA is approving this SIP revision because we find that it meets the applicable CAA requirements.

The special controls that apply to the device type are identified in this order and will be part of the codified language for classification of the digital cervical cytology slide imaging system with artificial intelligence algorithm. We are taking this action because we have determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of the safety and effectiveness of the device. We believe this action will also enhance patients' access to beneficial innovative devices, in part by reducing regulatory burdens.

articles.summary: The transpacific has become the most lucrative major container shipping trade in the world, with carriers generating five times more spot revenue per nautical mile on the Shanghai–Los Angeles route than on shipments to North Europe via the Cape of Good Hope. New analysis from Alphaliner shows that the extraordinary strength of the US trade …
articles.content: Transpacific emerges as liner shipping's golden trade - Splash247 Port of Long Beach The transpacific has become the most lucrative major container shipping trade in the world, with carriers generating five times more spot revenue per nautical mile on the Shanghai–Los Angeles route than on shipments to North Europe via the Cape of Good Hope. New analysis from Alphaliner shows that the extraordinary strength of the US trade has persisted well beyond the traditional peak season, with freight rates approaching levels last seen during the pandemic. At approximately $7,500 per feu, the 5,775 nautical mile Shanghai–Los Angeles voyage generates $1.30 in revenue per container per nautical mile, compared with just 26 cents on Shanghai–Rotterdam via the Cape, or 34 cents via Suez. Shanghai–New York generates 96 cents per nautical mile, with spot rates remaining above $10,000 per feu since late August. These figures represent revenue rather than profit, but nevertheless illustrate the extraordinary divergence between the industry’s principal east–west trades. Carriers are responding by throwing more tonnage at the Pacific. MSC recently upgraded its Sentosa service with 23,600 teu megamaxes, replacing vessels of approximately 15,000 teu. ZIM, which already deploys 52% of its capacity on the Pacific, will launch another China–California service in December. The boom is feeding directly into corporate earnings. COSCO reported third-quarter liner profits of $2.66bn, double the year-earlier

articles.content: Stronger revenue at Uber Freight, but profits still elusive - FreightWaves Uber Freight CEO Rebecca Tinucci took to LinkedIn to tout the company’s third quarter financial performance, which still is a long way from operating profitability. As Tinucci said in her published remarks, “two things can be true at the same time.” Her comments highlighted gross bookings of $1.768 billion, which is a record for the group. It also was a 34% improvement over the third quarter of 2026. Sequentially, Uber Freight (NYSE: UBER) revenue also was up from the second quarter figure of $1.583 billion, an 11.6% gain. But those higher revenues also came with another operating loss, $33 million. That wasn’t what Tinucci focused on in her LinkedIn remarks. Instead, she cited other statistics that were not in the Uber parent company’s prepared statement regarding its earnings. Tinucci said the approximately 35% year-over-year in revenue was “supported by an exceptional 36% volume increase in our U.S. & Canada brokerage.” She added that occurred even though the market featured “relatively flat freight volumes across the industry.” Revenue per load was up about 8% year-over-year, Tinucci said. Loads per day per head, considered in the brokerage business to be one of the key measures of productivity, was up about 10% from the third quarter of 2025. articles.content: Benelux returns to China for LPG carrier brace - Splash247 Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding Greek gas shipowner Benelux Overseas has been linked to another pair of midsize gas carriers at China’s Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding, adding to its growing orderbook at the CSSC-affiliated yard. Shipbuilding sources have identified the Athens-based company, controlled by Kostas Angelou, as the buyer behind the latest 48,000 cu m two-ship deal, extending a relationship dating back to late 2023. Huangpu Wenchong has confirmed the contract through China Shipbuilding Trading, identifying the customer only as a European shipowner. Pricing and delivery dates have not been disclosed. The conventionally fuelled vessels will be based on the yard’s established 48,000 cu m design, developed by Shanghai Merchant Ship Design and Research Institute (SDARI). The ships will feature three independent fully refrigerated Type A cargo tanks, allowing them to carry LPG and ammonia, among other cargoes. Benelux first turned to Huangpu Wenchong in December 2023, ordering two vessels of the same size with an option for a third, which was exercised in March 2024. The initial pair was reported to cost around $64m apiece. The first vessel from that programme, Olympios Gas (pictured), was completed in July this year. The latest deal adds to the Greek owner’s wider gas carrier expansion, which has also included a move into larger ammonia-capable tonnage. articles.content: Orkim books $38m product tanker pair in China - Splash247 Orkim Malaysian tanker owner Orkim has signed contracts for two more product tankers in China, committing about $37.6m as it presses ahead with fleet expansion following last year’s stock market listing. The Bursa Malaysia-listed company said its wholly owned subsidiary Orkim Marine entered into shipbuilding deals with Fujian Southeast Shipbuilding and Fujian Mawei Shipbuilding. The two 9,000 dwt clean petroleum product tankers are scheduled for completion by the end of 2028 and 2029, respectively, according to the stock exchange filing. The combined investment is equivalent to MYR153.6m. Orkim said it plans to finance the contracts through a combination of internal funds and borrowings, with the final financing structure depending on the timing and size of loan drawdowns. The latest contracts form part of a wider programme to add five more tankers between 2027 and 2029, including the previously contracted Orkim Ruby, a 14,500 dwt product carrier scheduled for next year. Orkim currently operates 21 vessels with a combined carrying capacity of 281,534 dwt, serving Malaysian and regional energy customers. The owner has been expanding its chemical and product tanker exposure since listing on Bursa Malaysia in December 2025. Earlier this year, it acquired the 13,850 dwt Rich Sunda for $24.2m and subsequently agreed to buy the 13,988 dwt Rong Yao Wu Zhou for CNY157m ($23.6m at today’s exchange rate). articles.content: First look: GXO Logistics Q3 revenue hits $3.6B - FreightWaves GXO Logistics reported third-quarter revenue of $3.59 billion, a 5.7% increase from a year earlier, as the global contract logistics provider secured more new business and expanded its sales pipeline to record levels. The Greenwich, Connecticut-based company (NYSE: GXO) said Tuesday that organic revenue grew 6.4% during the quarter ended Sept. 30, its fastest pace in more than three years. GXO also reported $375 million in new business wins, a 34% year-over-year increase and the second consecutive quarter in which new contract wins grew more than 30%. The company’s sales pipeline reached a record $3.1 billion, up more than 30% from a year earlier, signaling continued demand for outsourced warehousing, distribution and supply chain services. “The new strategy we put in motion over the past year is delivering results,” GXO CEO Patrick Kelleher said in a news release. Kelleher said the company is winning more business across its core markets and strategic growth sectors while improving its ability to convert opportunities into revenue. GXO Q3 financial performance GXO reported net income of $65 million, compared with $60 million during the same period in 2025. Diluted earnings per share increased to 56 cents from 51 cents. articles.content: Norway Detains Sanctioned Chinese Vessel Over False Flag Registration Ya Qing Hai Yang off Vesterålen Islands. (Courtesy of Arctic North Adventures) Norway Detains Sanctioned Chinese Vessel Over False Flag Registration Malte Humpert Total Views: 216 November 3, 2026 Norway has detained a Chinese-owned heavy-lift vessel sanctioned for its role in delivering equipment to Russia’s Arctic LNG 2 project, in what appears to be the first known detention in the Arctic of a Chinese vessel linked to Russia’s shadow fleet. The Ya Qing Hai Yang was detained after Norwegian inspectors found that it lacked valid flag-state registration and required certificates, the Norwegian Maritime Authority said. The case is a notable enforcement action against a vessel with documented ties to Russia’s sanctioned energy sector, although authorities say the detention was based on maritime safety and registration deficiencies rather than the ship’s sanctions status. The Norwegian Maritime Authority inspected the vessel on October 13 after it sought shelter from bad weather in Andfjorden, off the Vesterålen Islands in northern Norway. “During the inspection, it was discovered that the vessel did not have a valid flag registration and lacked the required certificates,” Dag Inge Aarhus, the authority’s communications director said last week. “The vessel has therefore been detained until further notice.” The vessel remains off the Vesterålen Islands as of November 3. articles.content: October deluge brings Panama Canal lake levels back towards normal - Splash247 Monjasa A surprisingly wet October has brought much-needed relief to the Panama Canal, with Gatun Lake recovering to near its historical average despite warnings that a powerful El Niño could trigger another prolonged drought. New research from Ursa Shipbrokers, drawing on Panama Canal Authority data, shows Gatun Lake averaged 85.80 ft (26.15 m) over the first 30 days of October, just 0.15 ft below its historical October average. The recovery is particularly striking compared with 2023, when severe drought crippled canal operations. October’s average was 6.04 ft higher than the corresponding month three years ago. The turnaround follows an unusually prolonged decline in lake levels, which continued until August this year rather than bottoming out in May, as is normally the case. Rainfall statistics underline the improvement. Data compiled from the canal authority’s meteorological stations show 303.3 mm of rain fell across the watershed between October 1 and 29, 8.4% above the 30-year average and 83.6% more than during the same period in drought-stricken 2023. By October 29, Gatun Lake’s daily level had reached 86.56 ft, up from an August low of 83.80 ft. Improved conditions have allowed the canal authority to reverse some restrictions. articles.content: Grimaldi lines up 10 car carrier newbuilds in China - Splash247 Grimaldi Italian shipping group Grimaldi is lining up another 10 car carriers at Chinese shipyards, including a series of 11,000 ceu vessels that would become the largest in its fleet. The Naples-based owner has signed letters of intent with China Merchants for five next-generation 10,000 ceu pure car and truck carriers (PCTCs) and with CSSC’s Guangzhou Shipyard International (GSI) for another five ships of 11,000 ceu each. Both designs will have additional capacity for containers and other rolling cargo, extending their capabilities beyond conventional vehicle transportation. The Emanuele Grimaldi-led owner confirmed the agreements, saying the projects would now move from preliminary design to engineering, a process expected to take around six months. Deliveries are targeted for 2030 and 2031. The agreements have yet to translate into firm shipbuilding contracts, with no pricing disclosed for the proposed vessels. The latest move builds on Grimaldi’s extensive car carrier expansion in China. In 2022 and 2023, the group amassed an orderbook of 17 ammonia-ready PCTCs (pictured), comprising 10 ships at China Merchants and seven at CSSC-affiliated yards. The owner has since been taking larger ships into its fleet, most recently the 9,800 ceu Grande Pacifico and Grande Egitto, built by China Merchants Heavy Industries Jiangsu. The post Mexico cargo thieves shift tactics as Q3 truck parking thefts surge appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Mexico cargo thieves shift tactics as Q3 truck parking thefts surge - FreightWaves Cargo thieves in Mexico are increasingly targeting parked trucks, shifting operations toward the country’s industrial heartland and exploiting nighttime security vulnerabilities. “Now, in Mexico, you can’t move loads without a plan,” Luis Enrique Villatoro, president of the Mexico-based National Association of Vehicle Tracking and Protection Companies (ANERPV). Supply chain risk management company Overhaul’s third-quarter 2026 cargo theft analysis found that thefts involving parked commercial vehicles accounted for 42.2% of reported incidents, up 9 percentage points from the same period last year. “There are some [parking lots] that are more insecure than others. And the status of safe havens is changing,” said Guadalajara, Mexico-based Ricardo Malacara, sales director at Overhaul. Thefts involving trucks intercepted while traveling declined 8.6 percentage points to 55.4% of incidents, signaling a significant shift in how criminal groups are targeting freight. The changing tactics present new challenges for trucking companies, manufacturers and logistics providers operating in Mexico, particularly those transporting goods through industrial corridors connecting central Mexico to the U.S. border. articles.content: Harbinger raises $240M to expand EV platform beyond trucks - FreightWaves Harbinger raised $240 million in Series D funding to push its electric vehicle platform into energy storage, power generation, autonomy, and defense while it ramps production for a 2,000-truck order from FedEx. The release describes Harbinger as “an American industrial technology platform company” and lists commercial vehicles as one of five markets the new funding covers. “Electrification is at the core of everything we do, and increasingly, electrification is at the core of industry, defense, mobility, and AI,” said John Harris, Harbinger’s co-founder and CEO, in the release. What Harbinger builds today Harbinger builds Class 4 through Class 6 chassis in all-electric and plug-in hybrid versions and designs its own powertrain, battery system, steering, and brakes. Its HC Series Cab, unveiled in March, adds a gasoline range extender good for up to 500 miles, depending on configuration, and up to 15 kilowatts of exportable power, so crews don’t need a separate generator. articles.content: Aker Solutions bags engineering deal for Qatar oilfield redevelopment - Splash247 Aker Solutions Norwegian offshore engineering group Aker Solutions has received a letter of award from Vietnam’s PTSC Mechanical & Construction for work on QatarEnergy’s Maydan Mahzam oilfield redevelopment project. The contract covers detailed engineering for three major topsides, four jackets and modifications required to connect new facilities with existing offshore infrastructure. Aker Solutions describes the award as sizeable, valuing it between NOK500m and NOK1.5bn ($54m to $162m). The company will carry out engineering work from its offices in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and Mumbai, India. The award remains subject to a final contract, with Aker Solutions expecting to register the order in its Renewables and Field Development segment during the fourth quarter of 2026. The Maydan Mahzam field lies around 100 km northeast of Qatar’s coastline, in water depths of approximately 40 metres. Discovered in the 1960s, the field began producing in 1965. QatarEnergy is undertaking a major redevelopment to modernise ageing offshore facilities, improve production efficiency and extend the field’s operating life. PTSC M&C secured the project’s first major offshore construction package in September and signed the main contract with QatarEnergy on October 22. articles.content: Mexico destroys 52 tons of avocados after pest discovery raises export concerns - FreightWaves Mexican avocado producers have destroyed up to 52 tons of fruit after authorities detected a destructive agricultural pest in shipments intended for international export to the U.S. and other destinations. The seed weevil pest raises concerns about potential disruptions to U.S.-Mexico avocado trade, which generates an estimated $641.5 million in cross-border transportation and warehousing activity. Environmental officials in Michoacán, Mexico’s largest avocado-producing state, confirmed Sunday that avocado seed weevil larvae had been discovered in fruit destined for export, according to Reuters. The discovery prompted authorities to detain shipments, while growers from Michoacán, Jalisco, Colima and Nayarit destroyed up to 52 tons of avocados over the weekend. Mexico’s National Service of Health, Food Safety and Food Quality (SENASICA) supported the disposal of the fruit as part of efforts to prevent the pest from spreading. Videos circulating on social media showed growers unloading truckloads of avocados into pits, where the fruit was burned and buried under pest-control protocols. The avocado seed weevil can damage fruit by boring into its seed and can spread through orchards, threatening production if infestations are not contained. The post Flexport forwarding volumes up 40% as headcount grows only 5% appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Flexport forwarding volumes up 40% as headcount grows only 5% - FreightWaves Flexport’s freight volumes are up 40% from a year ago while its headcount has grown 5%, founder and CEO Ryan Petersen told FreightWaves. He credits the gap to artificial intelligence tools the company now runs across customs, routing and its own engineering teams. The AI has a limit in customs, the most regulated part of Flexport’s business. There, an AI-generated tariff code still has to pass a licensed broker before it can legally reach U.S. Customs and Border Protection. “Our volumes are up 40% annually. And headcount’s only up 5%, so you can see the AI’s working,” Petersen said. The interview followed Flexport’s fall technology release, which added an AI classification tool to its customs software and rail, barge and air routing to its free Flexport Atlas map. Time magazine named Flexport’s Customs Technology Suite to its Best Inventions of 2026 list on Oct. 15. AI classification still needs a licensed broker Classifying goods under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule is “the hardest problem in customs,” Petersen said. Flexport’s new tool suggests a 10-digit code and links the CBP rulings behind it. Federal law limits who can do that work for someone else. In a Jan. 16 ruling, CBP found that a foreign online platform was conducting customs business when its AI tool derived tariff subheadings beyond the six-digit level for goods that would be entered. articles.content: Mexico widens US trade lead with record $96.3B September - FreightWaves Mexico remained the United States’ largest trading partner in September, with two-way commerce surging 34.2% year over year to a record $96.34 billion. According to the latest trade data analyzed by WorldCity, Canada ranked second with $64.78 billion in two-way trade, followed by China at $41.1 billion. Mexico accounted for 17.15% of total U.S. international trade during September. U.S. imports from Mexico totaled $62.24 billion, up 39.6% from $44.58 billion a year earlier. American exports to Mexico increased 25.4% to $34.09 billion, compared with $27.2 billion in September 2025. The figures reflect a sharp acceleration in cross-border commerce, particularly for manufactured goods, electronics and transportation equipment. Mexico’s trade growth also outpaced the broader U.S. international trade market, which increased 21.8% year over year to $561.82 billion in September. The U.S. merchandise trade deficit with Mexico reached approximately $28.15 billion for the month, based on the difference between reported imports and exports. articles.title: North America container imports rise 9% as as freight pricing pressures mount
articles.summary:
Global container volumes surged in September despite mounting disruptions and rising freight prices.
The post North America container imports rise 9% as as freight pricing pressures mount appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: North America container imports rise 9% as as freight pricing pressures mount - FreightWaves Global container volumes reached 17.35 million TEUs in September 2026, up 8% from a year earlier, as trade remained resilient despite mounting disruption and rising freight prices. Monthly liftings fell 1.4% from August, although the decline followed the highest monthly volume recorded in the Container Trade Statistics database. Year-to-date volumes remained 5% above the same period in 2025, maintaining the growth rate seen since June. North American imports increased 9% year-on-year, driven primarily by cargo originating in Asia and Europe. That marked an acceleration from the 7% annual growth recorded in the second quarter, extending the region’s recovery following weaker performance earlier in the year. For the third quarter, global container volumes totaled 52.2 million TEUs, an increase of 2.4% from the second quarter. The gains came as the industry continued to face geopolitical disruption, capacity constraints and higher operating costs. The Global Price Index rose to 123 points in September, up 5.1% from August and 62% above its September 2025 level. The increase pointed to pressure on container shipping even as cargo volumes continued to expand. Disruption to major shipping routes, constrained capacity and higher operating costs continued to influence pricing. articles.content: EnerMech picks up Chevron pipeline work off Equatorial Guinea - Splash247 EnerMech UK-headquartered oilfield services specialist EnerMech has secured a contract from Chevron for pipeline pre-commissioning services on the Aseng gas development offshore Equatorial Guinea. The contract covers preparation of approximately 19 km of rigid production flowline connecting the Aseng field to existing offshore infrastructure. EnerMech will provide pre-operational engineering, project management, and specialist pipeline pre-commissioning services, with the project managed from its Houston base. The award is part of Chevron’s wider Aseng Gas Monetization Project, which involves a single-well subsea tieback connecting the Aseng field to the existing Alen platform in water depths of around 800 m. Chevron made a final investment decision on the development earlier this year, and the project is expected to help sustain Equatorial Guinea’s LNG exports into the mid-2030s. Subsea 7 secured a separate installation contract worth between $150m and $300m in April. Its scope covers the transport and installation of the 19 km rigid production flowline, approximately 20 km of umbilicals, subsea structures, and associated tie-ins. EnerMech’s latest contract covers the specialist work required to prepare the pipeline infrastructure for operation.
